correctness.rationale: For six distinct roots a vanishing matching determinant gives rank two, with a relation having all coefficients nonzero, because the three pair quadratics have pairwise disjoint zeros. Scale to A+B+C=0 and use the displayed Q_i formulas. A single simple root of a difference gives discriminant order two and a nodal cubic with c4 nonzero, so a minimal I_2 fiber. The fundamental line bundle has degree one over P1, giving rationality; the cited converse covers every surface in scope. The trace-zero projective matrix equations are exactly the dependence test; even if one point lies in the kernel of a candidate rank-one matrix, the other two pairs prevent a constant projective map, so the matrix is invertible. A branch-fixed base involution has lifts of order four, whereas three exchanged pairs admit an order-two lift and a degree-two elliptic quotient. Each fixed-matching incidence divisor is irreducible by varying the involution in the trace-zero projective plane off the determinant conic and then varying three representatives. No diagonal is a component (the collision witness and relabeling suffice), and multidegree one in each root rules out a repeated component. The one-matching witness distinguishes all matching divisors by relabeling. The product transforms by a sign character, which cannot be alternating by the nonzero collision specialization. Descent gives degree fifteen, and on the distinct-root locus the quotient is étale, so multiplicity is one; transitivity gives one irreducible divisor. Its generic single matching reconstructs ordered differences up to common scale; relabeling the differences amounts to permuting the Q_i and possibly reversing their common sign. The resulting generically unique section-preserving coarse correspondence over C is birational. No assertion about special fibers or the boundary is needed.
